problem: Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ for $s>0,$ where $f(t)=u(8-t)$ and $u$ is the unit step function.$\,F(s)=L{f(t)}=$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the unit step function is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & t<0 \\ 1,\, & t\ge 0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
\begin{aligned}u(8-t)={\begin{aligned}1,\, & t\le 8 \\ 0,\, & t>8\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }u(8-t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{8}1\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{8}^{\infty }0\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{8}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We compute this integral for $s>0$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{8}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-\frac{{e}^{-st}}{s}]}_{0}^{8} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-8s}}{s}+\frac{1}{s} \\  & =\frac{1}{s}(1-{e}^{-8s})\end{aligned}
$$
